Algorithm analysis provides tools for reasoning about correctness and efficiency.

Big-O notation captures asymptotic growth: an algorithm is O(f(n)) if its
runtime grows no faster than cf(n) for sufficiently large n.

Common complexity classes, slowest to fastest growth: O(1) < O(log n) < O(n) <
O(n log n) < O(n²) < O(2ⁿ).
